articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation, Targets Shipping Services for Sanctions Evasion
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an update to its Iran designations, specifically modifying the listing for VOLTA SHIPPING SERVICES LLC.
The entity, also known as VOLTA CONTAINER LINE FZCO, is located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and is linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.
This action is part of ongoing efforts to counter Iran's sanctions evasion tactics, particularly within its shadow fleet and procurement networks.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses for Facilitating Iranian Sanctions Evasion
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight Canada-based money services businesses (MSBs) for operating in the digital asset sector of the Iranian economy.

These MSBs are accused of brokering transactions that convert Iranian rial and other currencies into crypto assets, thereby enabling Iran-linked international transactions and facilitating sanctions evasion.
Many of the designated firms reportedly transacted with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and crypto addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in Cyber, Transnational Crime, and Cuban Sectors
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in cyber-related malicious activities and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new Cuba-related designations.
The Cuba-related actions include a determination pursuant to Executive Order 14404, focusing on the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy.

The broader designations target global scam networks and their corporate infrastructure, including individuals and entities linked to the Cambodia-based Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Alert on Shadow Fleet and Amends Venezuela General License
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an Iran-related Alert titled "Iranian Shadow Fleet Reliance on False Flags for Sanctions Evasion."
Concurrently, OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 5AA, which authorizes certain transactions related to the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 Percent Bond on or after December 18, 2026.
Additionally, OFAC updated certain Iran-related listings on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List and amended Frequently Asked Question 595.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended General License for Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the issuance of Iran General License FF-1.
This amended general license authorizes the wind down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.
The action provides a limited period for the orderly cessation of certain activities with the specified entity.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities Tied to North Korea IT Worker Fraud and DRC Conflict
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in North Korea's illicit IT worker fraud schemes and those supporting destabilizing activities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Among the North Korea-related designations are Russian and North Korean nationals linked to entities such as LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY ALIS, CHINYONG INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY COOPERATION COMPANY, and FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER.

The DRC-related designations include the Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama Credit and Savings Society (Zigama CSS), a Kigali-based financial institution, for their alleged support of the M23 group.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a $1,529,685 settlement with Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-headquartered cloud networking solutions provider.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services on nine occasions from the United States to Joint Stock Company (JSC) Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer.
MMZA was blocked by operation of law due to its majority ownership by the designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even though MMZA itself was not directly listed on the SDN List until June 2022.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Frequently Asked Questions on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced amendments to several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) related to blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
The updated FAQs, including numbers 10, 32-36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, are part of OFAC's ongoing review to ensure its published guidance remains current.

These revisions clarify procedures for financial institutions regarding when to freeze funds, when to reject prohibited transactions, and the timing and documentation requirements for reporting to OFAC.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran and Russia General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, alongside the removal of certain Belarus and North Korea designations.

OFAC also issued Iran General License GG, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Karnakis and Karnakis, and Iran General License HH, for wind down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and offloading cargo involving certain blocked persons or vessels.

Additionally, Russia-related General License 131K was issued, authorizing certain transactions for the negotiation and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Chinese Entities Under PAIPA for Intellectual Property Theft, Issues General Licenses
body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).

These designations target five entities, including Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co Ltd (Zhisuan), Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd (MiraclePlus), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (Phase I), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (Phase II), and Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Zhiyuan Enterprise Management Center Limited Partnership (Zhiyuan Enterprise), in connection with the theft of trade secrets from U.S. persons.

OFAC also issued PAIPA General License 1, authorizing transactions pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations, and PAIPA General License 2, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving certain entities blocked on October 19, 2026.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
